title: U.S. House · North Carolina's 5th District
area: Northwestern North Carolina, including Boone, Wilkesboro and the northern foothills.

context.text: Chuck Hubbard won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary. Incumbent Virginia Foxx (R) won her Republican primary. Independent David Clayton did not make the general-election ballot. Robert Luffman advanced from a canceled Libertarian primary.

candidates.name: Virginia Foxx

summary.text: Virginia Foxx is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in North Carolina's 5th Congressional District. A former community college president and North Carolina state senator, she has served in the U.S. House since 2005 and chairs the House Committee on Rules; she previously chaired the Committee on Education and the Workforce.

background.text: Born in New York, New York, in 1943.
Earned a bachelor's degree and an M.A.C.T. from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1968, 1972) and an Ed.D. from the University of North Carolina at Greensboro (1985).

Began her career as a secretary and research assistant at UNC-Chapel Hill, then taught at Caldwell Community College and was a sociology instructor and assistant dean of the General College at Appalachian State University.
Served as Deputy Secretary for Management in the North Carolina Department of Administration under Gov. Jim Martin, and with her husband owned a nursery business in Watauga County.
Served on the Watauga County Board of Education (1976 to 1988, per Ballotpedia) and was president of Mayland Community College from 1987 to 1994.
Served in the North Carolina Senate from 1994 to 2004, then was first elected to the U.S. House in 2004 and took office in January 2005.

In Congress, served as Secretary of the House Republican Conference (2013 to 2016), chaired the Education and the Workforce Committee, and now chairs the Rules Committee. Her office says she authored the SKILLS Act (H.R. 803), which was combined with a Senate bill to form the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act signed in 2014.
According to her office, she has served on the National Advisory Council for Women's Educational Programs and on the Z. Smith Reynolds Foundation Advisory Panel, and is a lay leader in her church.

priorities.text: Opposing new federal gun restrictions as infringements on the constitutional right to keep and bear arms.
Securing the border, enforcing current immigration law, and requiring mandatory E-Verify for employment.
Fiscal conservatism, including opposing unnecessary federal spending and higher taxes and pursuing an "all of the above" energy policy.

positions.summary: Describes herself as a lifelong defender of Second Amendment rights and opposes new proposals she says would infringe on law-abiding citizens' right to keep and bear arms.
positions.quote: As a lifelong defender of Second Amendment freedoms, I am committed to ensuring that any new proposals considered in Washington do not infringe upon the constitutionally guaranteed rights of law-abiding citizens.

positions.summary: Says she shepherded H.R. 1, which she says funds border wall construction, expanded immigration court capacity and the deportation of criminal illegal aliens, and led the Laken Riley Act, which she says empowers law enforcement to detain illegal aliens.
positions.quote: This legislation puts Americans first by empowering law enforcement to build over 700 miles of border wall, deploy 1,670 miles of secondary barriers, expand immigration court capacity, hire critical staff, deport criminal illegal aliens, and more.

record.text: Chairs the House Committee on Rules and also serves on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (Government Operations Subcommittee) and the Committee on Education and the Workforce.
Chaired the House Committee on Education and the Workforce during the 118th Congress (2023-2025).

Positions are drawn from her official House issues pages, which describe her record from earlier Congresses but remain posted as her current statement of positions; an energy/gas prices issue page was also checked but described a general "all of the above" approach without naming opposition to clean-energy policy.

candidates.name: Chuck Hubbard
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary, defeating Kyah Creekmore.

summary.text: Chuck Hubbard is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Virginia Foxx in North Carolina's 5th Congressional District. According to his campaign website, he is a Wilkes County native who spent more than forty years as a local journalist at the Wilkes Journal-Patriot, the family-founded newspaper. He says he is running on affordability, public education, and protecting Medicare, Medicaid and Social Security.

background.text: Born in Bryson City, North Carolina; describes himself as a native of Wilkes County with family roots across the state.
Graduated from Wilkes Central High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Wofford College in 1985.

According to his campaign website, began working at age 8 in the print shop of the Wilkes Journal-Patriot, a newspaper founded by his grandfather, began covering news for it at 16 as a student, and joined full-time after college.
Worked as a journalist for more than forty years, according to his campaign website.
Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary for this seat, defeating Kyah Creekmore, 56.7% to 43.3%.

Has served on the boards of the Wilkes Recovery Revolution, the Wilkes Child Abuse Prevention Team and the Wilkes Prison Ministry; his campaign site says he lives with his wife Shari, who served over twenty years as a State Trooper, and they have three daughters and two grandchildren.

priorities.text: Addressing the rising cost of healthcare, housing, child care, groceries and utilities, and raising the minimum wage.
Supporting public education, teachers, and school infrastructure.
Protecting Medicare, Medicaid and Social Security benefits, and access to reproductive healthcare.

positions.summary: Says Congress must raise the minimum wage and shift more of the tax base to wealthy people and corporations to help working families get by.
Pledges to always vote to protect Medicare and Medicaid benefits that North Carolinians depend on.
Says he will always protect a woman's right to choose and access to critical reproductive healthcare.
His campaign platform says the tax base should shift more toward wealthy individuals and corporations.
positions.quote: we must shift the tax base more to rich people and wealth corporations

candidates.researchNotes: Hubbard has not previously held elected office; positions are drawn from his campaign website's platform statement as quoted by Ballotpedia.

candidates.name: Robert Luffman
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Libertarian Party primary.

summary.text: Robert Luffman is the Libertarian Party nominee in North Carolina's 5th Congressional District. He works in transportation and is a graduate of East Wilkes High School. In his Ballotpedia survey he says he opposes the two-party system and favors congressional term limits, pledging to seek no more than five terms.

background.text: Career experience includes working in transportation.
Advanced to the November ballot after the March 3, 2026 Libertarian primary was canceled.

priorities.text: Congressional term limits, saying he would only seek to serve up to five total terms himself.
Immigration reform, saying Congress has not meaningfully updated immigration law since 1996.
Marijuana legalization and record expungement for past marijuana charges.

candidates.researchNotes: Priorities from his 2025 Ballotpedia survey (no issue positions stated). His campaign site (luffmanforcongress.org) was loaded and contains no issue positions; no news questionnaire or debate coverage found.
